title: Count Substrings Without Repeating Character
summary: Given a string consisting only of lowercase English letters, count the number of substrings that do not contain any repeating characters.
statement: Given a string consisting only of lowercase English letters, count the number of substrings that do not contain any repeating characters. A substring is considered special if it contains no character that appears more than once. For example, in the string "pop", the substring "po" is special, but "pop" is not special. Return the total count of such special substrings.
constraints: Count nonempty substrings whose characters are all distinct.
Equal text at different positions counts as different substrings.
hints: Maintain the longest distinct-character window ending at each position.
Store each character’s latest index and move left past a duplicate without moving backward.
Add the current window length for every right endpoint.
Every valid substring ending at right starts at or after left, giving exactly right-left+1 new substrings.
editorial: Every valid substring ending at right starts at or after left, giving exactly right-left+1 new substrings.

tests.explanation: All ten substrings have distinct characters.
Only the three one-character substrings qualify.
